episodes.175948: A cold front caused a squall that resulted in several gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.177295: A frontal boundary crossed the Florida Peninsula on February 3rd. With the passage, thunderstorm winds were gusty in the late afternoon hours as storms traveled across the interior and Lake Okeechobee.
episodes.177379: Pre-frontal thunderstorm produced strong wind gusts near and over the adjacent marine waters.
episodes.177704: A major Arctic cold front blasted through southern New England on the morning of March 3rd. It was followed by a few rounds of strong and locally damaging wind gusts. Temperatures plunged to 10 to 20 below zero on the morning of March 4th. The -10F reading at Boston's Logan Airport was the coldest there since 1957.  Heavy freezing spray occurred, along with Arctic sea smoke.  Wind chill indices reached 30 to 40 below zero across southern New England.
episodes.177906: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Treasure Coast. Gale Warnings were in effect north of Sebastian Inlet.
episodes.178278: A convective cloud line developed rapidly between 3:00 pm EST and 5:00 pm EST just south of the lower Florida Keys, embedded in light west to northwest lower tropospheric flow with stronger westerlies aloft.  Convective available potential energy quickly increased to over 1,800 J/kg, likely enhancing the convective cloud growth unseasonably for early February.

events.county: Hawk Channel From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A brief, thin waterspout was observed by a trained spotter and NWS personnel west-southwest of Key West.  The waterspout was tilted at a 45-degree angle and the condensation cloud extended one-third of the way down from the cloud base to the horizon.  The waterspout moved slowly east-southeast and had a duration of about 3 minutes.  Over the following 90 minutes, six additional waterspouts were confirmed along a cloud line extending southeast to southwest of the far western Lower Keys.  A spray ring was visible with one waterspout as it passed south of Key West.  Most waterspouts were brief in duration, however one waterspout lasted for 25 minutes.  Most condensation clouds extended only a quarter of the way down from the cloud base.
At 609 PM EST, a Weatherflow mesonet site at Castle Island recorded a wind gust to 61 mph.
